title: Rust: Iterators and Combinators
description: Master Rust's iterator pattern with lazy evaluation and combinator methods.

steps.title: Basic Iterator Methods
steps.description: Create a Vec `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` and use `.iter()`, `.skip(2)`, `.take(2)` to get `[3, 4]`. Collect and print.
hints: Iterators are lazy — nothing happens until `.collect()` is called.

steps.title: Custom Iterator
steps.description: Implement the `Iterator` trait for a `Fibonacci` struct that generates Fibonacci numbers. Create an iterator that yields the first 10 Fibonacci numbers. Print them.
hints: `impl Iterator for Fibonacci { type Item = u64; fn next(&mut self) -> Option<u64> { let new = self.curr + self.next; self.curr = self.next; self.next = new; Some(self.curr) } }`

verification.failureMessage: Print the first 10 Fibonacci numbers using a custom iterator.

steps.title: Infinite Iterator with take
steps.description: Create an infinite iterator using `std::iter::repeat("Rust!")` and use `.take(3)` to get the first 3 values. Print them.
hints: This demonstrates the power of lazy iteration.

verification.failureMessage: Print 'Rust!' 3 times using repeat and take.

steps.title: Chain and Zip
steps.description: Use `.chain()` to concatenate two iterators, and `.zip()` to pair elements. Chain `[1, 2]` and `[3, 4]`, then zip with `["a", "b", "c", "d"]`. Print the pairs.
hints: Zip stops when the shorter iterator ends.

verification.failureMessage: Chain [1,2] and [3,4], zip with letters, print pairs.

steps.title: flatten and flat_map
steps.description: Given `[[1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6]]`, use `.iter().flatten()` to get a single sequence. Also use `.flat_map()` to transform and flatten in one step. Print both results.

verification.failureMessage: Flatten nested arrays and print both results.
